title: sdui-parser: port inert-quick-add and member-type-mismatch from objectui, re-record the lockstep and bump the pin
body:
Fixes #17645

Clause-②: yes

Executes the director-seat ruling in card comment 5714974800 (decision batch #146 item 3), maintainer's verbatim 「146 同意」 — **letter A**: port `inert-quick-add` and `member-type-mismatch` into this repo's `packages/sdui-parser`, re-record the lockstep and bump the pin in the same PR.

## Ported from

| | |
|---|---|
| repo | `objectstack-ai/objectui` (READ-ONLY clone in the dispatch container) |
| revision | **`cfcc17d9dd04ebb80c092cacb4f4034425f51b29`**, 2026-09-14T11:40:39Z |
| path | `packages/sdui-parser/src/{kanban-quick-add.ts,validate.ts,types.ts,index.ts,codegen.ts}` |

⚠️ That clone is **3 days older than the card's own reading** (the card measured objectui on 2026-09-16). What that means for the lockstep record is stated under "What the record cannot see" below — it is a real bound, not a formality.

## What each code actually guards

A reviewer should be able to tell a real port from a string copied across an enum. Neither code is a new red gate: both are warnings, so `compile().ok` — the save gate's pass/fail — is unchanged and a page that saves today still saves.

### `inert-quick-add` (objectui#8285)

`quickAdd` on the `object-kanban` tag reaches no control. The Quick Add button is gated on **both** halves of a pair — `quickAdd` **and** an `onQuickAdd` handler — and `onQuickAdd` takes a FUNCTION, which no page on this tier can write (this tier parses, it never executes; a handler attribute draws `forbidden-attr`) and which the board substitutes none of its own for.

It **replaces** the diagnostic the prop walk used to emit for that key rather than joining it. The old reading was `unknown-prop`, "has no prop quickAdd" — **false against the published contract**, because `ComponentPropsMap` for that tag does publish `quickAdd`. An author who checked the spec found the warning contradicted, concluded the manifest was behind the spec, and kept a key that will never do anything; it also could not be told apart from a typo. Two diagnostics for one mistake is the shape `checkMemberTypes` already refuses, so this one `continue`s the walk.

It is asked **ahead of the declaration lookup on purpose**: the claim is about the render path, which a declaration cannot change, so declaring `quickAdd` must not silently disarm it. Three things it deliberately does NOT fire on — a falsy value (the renderer's own gate is `quickAdd && onQuickAdd`, so the author got what they wrote), a braced value this tier never evaluates (opaque here), and any tag outside the one surviving host registration. Each has a control row in the tests.

### `member-type-mismatch` (objectui#8067)

The coarse type check **one level down**, over the member kind an input declares. `type: 'array'` said a value was a list and stopped there, so a member that drifted from the contract was invisible to every layer that reads a declaration.

This is the half that makes it a port and not a string: the code needs a key that did not exist in this copy at all. The change brings `ManifestInput.of` and **all three of its readers**:

- **the validator** — any declared arm accepting a member clears it; a member no arm accepts is reported, as ONE diagnostic naming every offending position, at `error` severity when an `enum` arm is present and `warning` otherwise;
- **the serializer** — `manifestFromConfigs` canonicalizes `of` exactly as it canonicalizes `type`, and publishes NO `of` for an input that declares none (routing `undefined` through `canonicalizeInputType`, whose no-arms fallback is `'string'`, would make every array in every manifest claim string members it was never told it had);
- **the codegen** — a declared member kind narrows the emitted element type, so the `.d.ts` an author type-checks against and the manifest gate agree.

The member walk runs only once the CONTAINER kind was accepted, so a wrong container draws one diagnostic and not two.

## Counts, each with a firing control

Base for every diff reading: `51297e9ee17db23f50d38c1431f5a4dcc47632ff`.

**Diagnostic codes — 26 = 26, sets identical element-for-element.** Measured with the gate's own AST extractor (`fingerprintOf`), both trees, before and after:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| this repo | 24 | **26** |
| objectui @ `cfcc17d` | 26 | **26** |

The delta was exactly `inert-quick-add` and `member-type-mismatch` — matching the card's 26/24 reading, so acceptance item 4 is met and nothing was absorbed.

**The grammar region did not move across the pin hop.** This repo's `parse.ts` region and objectui's at `cfcc17d` are both 214 lines, blob `0131f27cf86dbabec09b4ae55ae131403667e7e9` — byte-identical, and identical to what the old record held at `53ded82bf`. So the pin bump ports no grammar change.

**`of` declarations in the tracked manifest: 0 of 339 inputs.** FIRING CONTROL on the same file: the term `"inputs"` occurs 57 times in `sdui.manifest.json`, and `git diff BASE HEAD -- sdui.manifest.json | grep -c '"inputs"'` reads **0** — the whole-file diff is **0 bytes**. So the zero is a reading about the tree, not an artifact of this diff. The discriminating contrast: the same grep for `of?:` over `git diff BASE HEAD -- packages/sdui-parser/src` reads **2**, so the term is one this diff really moves where it moved it.

⚠️ Read that 0-of-339 honestly: `member-type-mismatch` has **no firing input in today's shipped manifest**, because that manifest is generated from the PUBLISHED `@object-ui/*` 17.6.0 packages, which predate the `of` declarations. It is NOT inert — objectui's SOURCE at `cfcc17d` declares `of` in 38 places (e.g. the tabs and panels `items` inputs in `containers.tsx`), so those flow in at the next publish+pin, and the reader is pinned here through the real serializer rather than a hand-built fixture. Without this port, this repo's save gate would silently accept member drift that objectui's renderer reports.

**objectui was never written to.** `git status --porcelain` in that clone: 0 files. `HEAD` still `cfcc17d9dd04ebb80c092cacb4f4034425f51b29`.

## Ablation ledger

Three ablations, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` — anchor declared and required to HIT, before/after anchor counts, `git hash-object` blob ids either side, restore proven by `blob == HEAD` AND an empty `git diff HEAD`, with an EXIT/INT/TERM trap. The tests resolve the subject through `src` (a relative intra-package import, no `dist` hop), which is why these run without a rebuild — measured: the suite passed before `dist` existed in this worktree at all.

| # | mutation | anchor | blob | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | disarm `checkKanbanQuickAdd`'s key guard | 1 → 0 | `0d5131868ace` → `99d89132858e` | **4 failed / 8 passed** |
| 2 | make the validator's member check read no declared arms | 1 → 0 | `156a264073f7` → `5cb7912d7f54` | **7 failed / 14 passed** |
| 3 | make the codegen narrow no member type | 1 → 0 | `76a7d654f1fd` → `ba55afbc8c19` | **3 failed / 18 passed** |

In each case the failures were exactly the SUBJECT rows and every control row stayed green — which is the split the control rows exist to produce. A first attempt at ablation 1 was REFUSED by the tool because the replacement still contained the anchor (count 1 → 1, "not the declared drop"); it is recorded here because the refusal is the tool working, and the run that produced the reading above is the corrected one.

## The pin bump, and its second and third halves

`.objectui-sha`: `53ded82bf7a494f54e344e19099dbf00854b8694` → `cfcc17d9dd04ebb80c092cacb4f4034425f51b29`.

**Second half — the manifest — is done and is a no-op in content.** `node scripts/gen-sdui-manifest-node.mjs --objectui-version 17.6.0` regenerates `sdui.manifest.json` **byte-identical**: sha256 `49211fee7792cf51` before and after. Both pins ship `@object-ui/*` **17.6.0**, so the published registry inputs did not move; only the record's `objectuiSha` and `generatedAt` follow the pin. `check-sdui-manifest` is green.

**Third half — `check:objectui-pin-citations` — is RED and is NOT closed by this PR.** See "Acceptance notes".

## What the record cannot see

`check-sdui-lockstep` compares this tree against a VENDORED record of objectui's side. It can see this copy drifting from the recorded objectui state; it **cannot** see objectui moving AFTER the record was taken. This record was taken at `cfcc17d` (2026-09-14) — and the card's own reading of objectui is from 2026-09-16. **Anything that landed in objectui's `packages/sdui-parser` in those two days is outside this record and outside this PR's evidence.** The gate says so itself on every green run, and only a later pin bump brings the question back. The container's objectui clone is shallow with exactly one commit, so this cannot be narrowed here.

## Gates

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` derived **67** families for this diff; re-derived after `git fetch` and the list was IDENTICAL, so the tool's STALE TREE warning does not move the answer. Reconciled with `--ran` recording every exit code: **67 derived, 64 run, 3 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN** (exit 0).

- `check:sdui-lockstep` — **green**, both the gate and `--self-test`: byte-identical over 214 grammar lines and agreeing on all 26 codes. ⛔ The invariant was never relaxed to buy this: `--update` re-reads OBJECTUI's side only and never this tree's parser, so it cannot record "whatever we have now"; the green is the port being faithful.
- `check:sdui-manifest` — green (present, intact, fresh at the new pin).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/sdui-parser test && … typecheck` — green, **176 tests / 10 files**.
- `check:nul-bytes` — green; plus a direct control-byte sweep over the changed files.
- `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` — was RED on this port and is now green; see "The one deliberate divergence".
- 3 families are **NOT MEASURED, not passes**: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt` each exited **3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET** (they need a full `pnpm build`), which is neither a pass nor a failure.
- `check:query-options-erasure` — green at 192s; an earlier 124 was this runner's own 150s timeout, not a finding.
- **`check:objectui-pin-citations` — RED, deliberately left open.** See below.

## The one deliberate divergence from objectui

objectui stamps `code: INERT_QUICK_ADD`. This copy stamps the inline literal `code: 'inert-quick-add'` and keeps the exported constant. This is not drift and not a shortcut — it is the same documented divergence `unconsumed-widget-option` already carries next door: `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary`'s `objlitconst` shape must reduce a constant at a `code:` position to a literal, and its literal grammar cannot admit a kebab-case value, so the constant form is an unresolvable-constant finding that cannot be declared away. The gate caught this port doing it, which is the gate working.

⛔ It does not weaken the lockstep: that gate resolves an identifier at a code position through the package's own module-level constants, so **both spellings reduce to the same code** and the two copies still agree on all 26. A test row pins the literal equal to the constant so the two cannot drift apart.

## Changeset

**OWED, and measured** rather than assumed — `.changeset/17645-sdui-parser-lockstep-port.md`, `minor`. The criterion is whether anything PUBLISHED moves: `@objectstack/sdui-parser` ships `files: ["dist", …]`, and after a build both codes are present in the shipped bytes, against a negative control that reads zero everywhere:

| symbol | index.js | index.mjs | index.d.ts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inert-quick-add` | 3 | 3 | 2 |
| `member-type-mismatch` | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| `checkKanbanQuickAdd` | 4 | 3 | 3 |
| `unconsumed-widget-option` (positive control) | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| `NEVER_SHIPPED_CONTROL_STRING` (negative control) | 0 | 0 | 0 |

That reading is also the answer to the Clause ② question the card asked to have re-judged if it measured otherwise: **these codes DO reach a published surface**, so the `needs:contract-review` declaration stands. The package's exported API grows by four symbols and one optional type key, which is why this is `minor` and not `patch`.

## Acceptance notes

**`check:objectui-pin-citations` is RED and this PR does not close it — this needs a decision.**

The pin bump invalidates **26 `packages/spec/**` sources** that cite `.objectui-sha` as "the pin this repo builds against" alongside hand-derived objectui `file:line` anchors. The gate refuses the cheap repair in terms: ⛔ "Do NOT fix this by replacing the sha… The sha is not the record — the objectui file:line ANCHORS beside it are, and they are only true of the tree they were counted in." Rewriting the sha alone would turn a loud, accurate "unverifiable" into a silent, confident lie.

Two reasons it is not done here, both measured:

1. **It is outside this card's binding file surface.** The claim comment declares `packages/sdui-parser/`, `scripts/`. Re-measuring 26 spec sources of hand-written cross-repo provenance prose is not a bounded in-place fix.
2. **The re-measure is not performable in this container.** Each record carries a "which anchors moved across the hop" narrative, which needs BOTH pin trees. The only objectui checkout here is **shallow with exactly one commit**: `git cat-file -t cfcc17d9dd04…` answers `commit`, while the old pin `53ded82bf7a4…` answers "could not get object info" — a firing control on a present object, so the absence is real. Deepening it would mean git WRITES inside a READ-ONLY checkout belonging to someone else, which is exactly what `check-sdui-lockstep`'s own header declines to do for the same reason.

So this is a genuine third half of "bump the pin" that letter A did not price. Landing it needs either a follow-up card scoped to `packages/spec/**` with a non-shallow objectui checkout, or a maintainer ruling. ⛔ Not absorbed silently, and #17645 is the only card this PR closes.

Other observations, noted and not filed — neither is a defect, and no PR or person is queued on either file, so there is no taker to hand them to:

- `packages/sdui-parser/src/provenance.ts` exists in objectui and not here. It is deliberately out of scope: it stamps zero diagnostic codes, so the lockstep's code-set comparison is unaffected (26 = 26 with it absent), and the gate does not compare file lists.
- objectui's `index.ts` also exports `assertFullyLoaded` and its codegen emits an `eslint-disable` banner; neither is part of either ruled code and neither is carried here.
